narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 26% chance you would become a bad credit risk. Although that is below half, it was still above the bank’s approval threshold for this loan. The three strongest factors shaped this result. The most influential was having a guarantor. This worked in your favor: it was the single strongest signal reducing the bad-risk estimate, so it helped your case. The next most important was the short 12-month repayment period. Because approved applicants typically request about 19 months, your shorter term also worked in your favor, lowering the risk estimate. The third and only adverse top factor was your checking account being below zero. Approved applicants rarely show this pattern—only about 12.6% have a negative balance—so this raised the risk estimate and pushed against approval. Even though two of the three most important factors helped you, the negative checking balance, combined with smaller adverse factors, kept your overall score above the bank’s limit. To improve future chances, bring your checking account balance to at least zero before reapplying, keep the loan term short if you can, and consider adding documentation of steady income or savings. You may also ask the bank whether a smaller loan amount or a co-applicant would help. Correcting the account status is the clearest actionable step.
